feature: Two-way effect settings are segmented controls
summary: A shadow's Kind (Drop or Inner), a glow's Kind (Outer or Inner), a label border's Follows (Letters or Box) and a saved style's Kind now show both answers side by side. One click switches them, with no dropdown to open.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Type a label with the Text tool (T), press Command-Return, and look at its Shadow in the Effects list: Kind shows Drop and Inner side by side.
Click Inner, then Drop, then press Command-Z once: the shadow goes back to Inner.
Add a Glow and a Border from the plus on the Effects header, then click Outer or Inner on the glow and Letters or Box on the border.
Make a second label, switch one label's shadow to Inner, and pick both in the Layers list: Kind lights neither segment and says Mixed.
Click Drop: both shadows turn Drop. Press Command-Z once and the Mixed comes back.
Drag the dock's left edge as narrow as it goes and look at Follows and Kind.
Save a shadow as a style (its Style menu, Save as Style), open it in the Library's Styles shelf, and click Inner or Drop under Kind.

evaluate: Is one click on the other word quicker than the dropdown it replaced?
Does Mixed beside the name read clearly enough when no segment is lit?
At the narrowest dock, is Letters | Box too tight against the panel edge?
Is it right that a border's Position (Inside, Center, Outside) is still a dropdown in the Effects list but a segmented control on a saved style?
rough: Matches the fields mock (comp-fields.html section 05: two to four choices are a segmented control), drawn as the app's one segmented control (UX-PATTERNS: The one segmented control).

A border's Position stays a dropdown in the Effects list: its three words need about 146pt and the effect row's control column is about 122pt at the dock's default width and about 80pt at its narrowest. Settled by UX-PATTERNS, The one segmented control (a dropdown in its place when the words would be cut short) and this task's own checklist.

On a saved style, Position is a segmented control: there the control runs the whole width of the dock, so three words fit even at the narrowest. The two places now look different for the same question.
Masked by stays a dropdown: it lists the layers below, so it can hold any number of choices. Settled by UX-PATTERNS §3 and the fields mock's rule that five or more choices are a select.
Mixed is drawn as UX-PATTERNS §4 What Mixed looks like says: the word beside the row's own name, no segment lit.
Current also changes: it draws these rows as the system's segmented picker, the way it draws every other segmented row, where yesterday's change had given it the panel dropdown.
